_comment: Cost-and-heterogeneity scaled CPM: 80^3 / t=1001, ~33s per simulation against
3.7s at 50^3. The point is the MECHANISM, not just the cost.
At 50^3 the measured advantage is 2.33x but the straggler ceiling is only
1.27x (runtime CV 0.05), so most of it is pyABC per-generation overhead --
which shrinks at production scale -- rather than barrier idle, which is what
the paper claims. Runtime correlates 0.99 with cell count, and at 80^3 the CV
rises to 0.26-0.47, putting the straggler ceiling at 1.90-2.90x. This run
measures which mechanism actually dominates when the simulation is realistic.
Assets are all 80^3 variants; the feature-space model is REFITTED on the 80^3
corpus because the shipped one was fitted where log_n ~ log(50) against
log(313) here. Priors and truths are the Route-E screen's calibrated band
tol_init 0.1 carried over from the 50^3 sweep; the block-normalised distance
should be on a similar scale, and the companion prior corpus checks it.
